the following: 1) the replacement of empirical data with the predicted values of phys/chem properties, 2) the replacement of the single-threshold approach with the approach taking into account uncertainty in the results.
the development of new methods and approaches for risk assessment of chemicals, and the improvement of the existing ones.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the QSPR-prediction of phys/chem properties for multimedia models is a valid approach and that it can be applied in risk assessment procedures for environmental chemicals.
the use of the QSPRs in the multimedia models does not significantly influence the results and, thus, the conclusions drawn from them.

the replacement of empirical phys/chem parameters with the QSPR-prediction ones in multimedia models does not lead to any statistically significant differences in the results obtained from the models.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the replacement of empirical data with those calculated from QSPRs does not affect the performance of the multimedia mass balance model, and that this approach can be recommended for use in the risk assessment procedures.
the QSPR-prediction of the phys/chem data in the multimedia models can be recommended for the risk assessment of chemicals.
QSPRs could be used as reliable alternative to the empirical phys/chem parameters in multimedia mass-balance models for environmental risk assessment of chemicals.
The main takeaway from our work is that
QSPRs are ready to be employed in risk assessment of environmental persistence and long-range fate of potentially hazardous chemicals.
the QSPR-based approach can be successfully employed to reduce the time and costs associated with risk assessment procedure.
the use of QSPRs in multimedia mass balance model can be recommended for risk assessment purposes.
